sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.note: Bibliographic inventory only. Entry 231 'Kakanda cluster' (dialects Kakanda-Budon, Kakanda-Gbanmi/Sokun) lists a single reference: 'Phonology: Oyebade (1988)' = the Ilorin MA thesis.
Stub citing Blench 2013 and Blench 2019 Atlas; no phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2013. The Nupoid languages of west-central Nigeria: overview and comparative word list. Working document (Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation), 100+ pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.3 item 8 Kakanda: 'The tone-system has not been described, but it appears to have three level tones.' sec. 2.3 Tone (p.8): all Nupoid languages studied have three level tones plus two glides. Kakanda otherwise appears only in wordlists and a remark on surface long vowels (p.6).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 1989. Nupoid. In John Bendor-Samuel (ed.), The Niger-Congo Languages, 305-322. Lanham: University Press of America.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. sec. 14.3.3 Tone (pp.314-315): 'All Nupoid languages studied to date have at least five surface tones, three level tones, and two glides'; Kakanda appears in the sound-correspondence figure 14.4 and vowel remarks only.

sources.note: The only phonological description of Kakanda on record (Glottolog 5.1 listed by Glottolog as a phonology; sole reference in Blench's 2020 Atlas entry). An autosegmental phonology from Ilorin in 1988 will have a tone chapter and is the one place a statement on stress/accent (or its absence) could exist.
